System 3 · Phase 6

How one build phase runs

Redesigned 2026-09-24, when you accepted all eight decisions in docs/build/Bossman_mode_redesign.md. Work is picked by what a person sees first, every phase fits in 8 hours and 8 agents, review stops at two rounds, and every phase ends on the deployed develop app, where a product reviewer looks before you do.

Who is in the room

Product owner You Merge the PR, retest on develop. Your verdict is the only thing that sets done. You talk only to the lead.
Tech lead Me, depth tier Pick the phase, split it by file, write each ticket's acceptance in your words, decide, report. Never writes the code it will judge.
Builders Balance tier One ticket, one file fence, the tests for it. Never dispatches an agent, never edits outside the fence.
Clerk Speed tier Board rows, counts, the handoff file, doc sync, by copying fields. Never restates a fact in its own words.
Judge Depth tier, one round Correctness, security, the production gates, and "break it, does a test go red". Never closes its own findings.
Adversary Depth tier, one round Hunts the confident wrong answer and the lying trust signal on any runnable change. Files, never closes.
Product reviewer A script captures, depth judges Drives develop at 1280 and 390 beside the prototype, asks the golden questions, reads answers against a five-line rubric. Closes nothing.

The phase loop

1
Pick and open the phaseleaddepth · high

Pick by what a person sees first: a wrong or missing answer, then a slow one, then a screen that looks wrong. Section 25 still says what a phase delivers and which dependencies are real, so a real dependency still goes first. Read the handoff file rather than rebuilding state from the board.

HANDOFF.md Technical_specification.md §25 Plan.md Phase 7
2
Read what already brokeleaddepth · low

Filter the learnings log to this phase, its tools, and its layers before scoping anything. Past dead ends are cheaper to read than to rediscover.

LEARNINGS.md, filtered
3
Split by file fenceleaddepth · high

Every ticket names the exact files it may touch and no two share a file. Each carries one acceptance sentence in your words and the test command that proves it. Before ticketing any screen, the lead reads the design coverage table, so a surface with no design is named as a gap rather than invented.

docs/build/design/README.md tracker/phase_N.M.md
4
Preflight and dispatchleaddepth · low

Probe each transport, cut phase/N.M-description, and plan the 8 dispatches before the first one, so the review round never runs out. Each builder gets its ticket, its fence, the files it needs and the learnings that name them, and nothing else: no history, no board, no conversation, no permission to dispatch.

git branch
5
Builders work in parallelbuildersbalance · medium

Each claims a ticket and sets it to in progress the moment it picks it up. Concurrent writers each get their own worktree. A builder that finishes sets in review, never done. Anything that breaks is written to the learnings log the moment it happens.

source and tests tracker/phase_N.M.md, own ticket only LEARNINGS.md
6
Judge, adversary, one fixjudge, adversarydepth · high

One judge round with cited evidence for every claim, then one adversary round on anything runnable, then one fix-and-verify: one fix agent per file, and a fresh verifier, never the judge. If it still blocks, the phase stops and you get two options, merge with the open item named or revert. There is no third round, even if you would authorise one. If more than half of a round's findings are about the phase's own tests, the phase stops writing checks and escalates.

the diff, the tests tracker/phase_N.M.md, Findings
7
Gates, in orderleaddepth · medium

verify, then eval-harness when answer generation was touched, then dev-standards when code shipped, then the learnings coverage check. The judge grades the work; these decide whether it is allowed to ship.

test and check output
8
Checkpoint and PRlead, clerkspeed · low

Tickets stay at in review. The checkpoint says what you will notice, in your words, what merges open, and the budget used: hours of 8, dispatches of 8, rounds of 2. Then docs sync, commit, push, and the pull request.

tracker/BOARD.md HANDOFF.md pull request
9
You mergeproduct ownerhuman

You read the checkpoint, not the diff, and merge. Develop deploys.

the pull requestthe board
10
Product reviewproduct reviewerscript, then depth · medium

Every changed screen on develop at 1280 and 390 beside the prototype, with a horizontal overflow check. On an answer-path change, the 50 golden questions three times each: any drop in the answered count stops everything else landing until it is fixed or reverted. Then the answers are read against five lines: does the first sentence answer, would a researcher learn something, do the two depths differ, how long did it take, does each screen match its design.

prototype/app.html run_consistency.py testing/Developer/reports
11
You retestproduct ownerhuman

You retest on develop with the product review as the list of what to look at first. Your verdict sets done, or sends defects back to the builders under the same budget.

the product review

BudgetLimitOn hitting it

Instrument shareover halfStop writing checks and escalate
Answer rateany dropStop and fix, or revert, before anything else lands

Which model runs where

These are build-time capability tiers, assigned to the agents that write System 3 itself. They are a separate concept from the product's own guard, plan, and synth runtime tiers, which route models per user query at serve time. Both are called tiers, but they name different things. The rule for the build-time tiers: spend reasoning where a mistake is expensive and cascades, spend cheaply where the task is bounded and the instructions are clear.

RoleTierEffortWhy this tier
Tech leaddepthhigh, low for routine stepsA bad split cascades into every builder downstream. The most expensive place to be wrong.
BuilderbalancemediumBounded construction against clear acceptance.
ClerkspeedlowMechanical copying of fields. Restating in its own words is how false sentences got in.
JudgedepthhighA missed defect here ships. A weaker review has cost whole rounds.
AdversarydepthhighFinding a fluent, plausible, wrong answer needs real adversarial reasoning.
Fix agentbalancemediumBounded repair of named findings, one agent per file.
VerifierdepthhighIt re-derives the judge's verdicts from scratch.
Product reviewerdepthmediumIt does your kind of judgement; a script does the capture.

Provider mapping

Two providers, three capability bands each, and an identical five-rung effort ladder. This table is the only place a provider name appears on this page. Every tier named above, and every model chip in the phase loop, points back to a row here.

TierWhat it is forClaudeCodex
depthArchitecture, hard debugging, long messy agentic work with many tradeoffsOpusSol
balanceNormal development work, bounded construction, careful checkingSonnetTerra
speedQuick lookups, extraction, classification, repetitive workHaikuLuna

Effort ladder, identical on both providers: low, medium, high, extra high, max. Raise the rung as the task gets harder, low for quick and bounded work, max for the one hardest problem where maximum depth matters most. Switching the harness to a different provider means editing this one table and nothing else, which is the property that makes the harness portable.

Where this can still go wrong

Known weak points, stated rather than hidden

The golden run's outcomes vary between runs of one question. Three passes reduce that noise and do not remove it, so only you may accept a drop.

The golden run counts answered questions, not correct ones. A fluent wrong answer still counts as answered; the rubric read and your retest are what catch it.

The product review runs after merge, because develop is the only deployment a branch reaches. A drop blocks further landings and forces a fix or a revert; it cannot stop the merge that caused it.

A board edit made through a shell command instead of the Edit tool bypasses the sync hook and leaves your page stale. Mitigated by re-rendering at phase close, not eliminated.

What this costs you

Three touchpoints per phase: a checkpoint to read, a pull request to merge, and a retest on develop with the product review in hand. Between those, nothing needs you unless a budget is hit or something blocks, and a blocked stop is a clean end state rather than a failure to hide. Build mode and the UI fix loop merge into one cadence with a risk dial after the next build phase.
